suggestions.why: This is the paragraph where you asked what the over-excitement was. The answer went in: the feeling follows the circuit the rise reaches, the amygdala, which is why it comes out as threat and not as joy. Then I rewrote it your way, payoff first in each sentence, terms glossed in place, the short sentences joined, and it read [AI at 100% in three windows](https://www.pangram.com/history/4026db4c-d192-4673-8adc-c56d711b8087). My version is in the card below this line.  What I can't get is the voice of a mechanism paragraph: every sentence of mine lands as a finished step with its citation, and both panel readers said the same thing about the rhythm.
suggestions.advice_note:
If you fix this one, the move I'd carry to blocks 39, 40 and 41, which read AI too ([39](https://www.pangram.com/history/60a9335d-05f1-4227-a6e4-9956415a2a71), [40 and 41](https://www.pangram.com/history/4312584e-a4de-471b-aaba-5459ffaa4cd9)), is whatever you do to break that step-by-step rhythm. Here is my try, to edit or to ignore:

The Mechanism: When glutamate floods in, it jams open the NMDA receptors, the doors glutamate opens on a brain cell, like a key stuck in the "On" position, and calcium pours in through them. Calcium that high kills the cell only in extremes, a stroke or a brain injury, and that killing is what "excitotoxicity" means (Sattler & Tymianski, 2001), so a storm doesn't mean your neurons are dying. What you feel comes from where the glutamate lands, and under stress it rises in the amygdala, the part that flags threats (Wilson, 2015), so an amygdala firing too hard hands you threat: anxiety, rage, the "itchy brain", and never joy. Block the NMDA receptors there and anxious behaviour drops in animals (Boyle, 2013).

suggestions.why: This is the clearest comparison we have. On 7 November you turned this paragraph Human with three moves on the old science: "well" for "according to", uncompressing the last sentence, and the question as the opener. I kept all three, carried the corrected claims in (GluD is a channel, the leak is what shows up in people, the armor part is a guess with a mechanism), ran the tell panel, cut everything the two readers agreed on, and it still read AI at High across the whole paragraph. So what carries your voice in this paragraph isn't those three moves on their own, and I can't see what it is.
suggestions.advice_note:
This is the one I'd most like you to fix, because it is the same paragraph you already fixed once, so your two versions side by side would show me what I lost when the claims changed. Mine is below, and the claims in it are the ones you approved, so keep those and change the words:

The Signal Dial (GluD Receptors): So if NMDA is the spark, what sets the level? Well, Johns Hopkins researchers recently found that GluD receptors, until now just the things that help build synapses, are channels themselves, and what opens them is D-serine (one of the tools below) and GABA, the chemical that quiets a cell down, not glutamate (Wang, et al, 2025). In people, what turns up is a leak. The mutation behind one inherited ataxia leaves the channel stuck open, and a gene variant that raises the risk of schizophrenia does too (Allen, et al, 2023), so the synapse never gets quiet. My guess is that an armored state jams it the same way, stuck part-way on, so you never come down to a baseline, which from the inside is hyper-vigilance. Nobody has tested that in trauma, so it stays a guess, though the lab already has a drug that shuts these leaking channels.
